paragraphs: Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend. Joseph walks in front of the most powerful man in Egypt, fresh out of a dungeon, and Pharaoh basically says, "I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream you can interpret it." Joseph could have grabbed that spotlight with both hands. Instead he says, "I myself cannot do it, but God will give Pharaoh a sound answer." (Genesis 41:15-16)

That's the lesson, baker. The wisdom was never Joseph's to brag about, and the magicians and wise men couldn't produce it either. Joseph says it plainly: "God has revealed to Pharaoh what He is about to do." (Genesis 41:25) God is the One who knows what's coming, and He's the One who tells it.

And look at what Joseph does with that. He doesn't just announce the bad news and walk off. He lays out a plan to prepare during the good years so the land will not perish. (Genesis 41:33-36) I'm still learning that one myself, because getting ready while things are calm is a lot harder than getting ready when the oven is already on fire. So listen to God's Word now, friend, and stay ready, because there's more of this story still to come.
